if.example: If '{{'steps.ping.status'}}' is 200, stop; otherwise wait and try again.

loop.name: Loop
loop.description: Repeats its steps a number of times, for each item of a list, or while a condition holds.
loop.example: Three times: call the restart API and wait 20 seconds.

parallel.name: Parallel
parallel.description: Runs 2 to 4 branches at the same time and waits for all of them.
parallel.example: Check the NAS and the router together.

workflow.name: Call workflow
workflow.description: Runs another workflow with inputs and gets its variables back.

stop.name: Stop
stop.description: Ends the whole run as succeeded or failed, with a reason.

set.name: Set variable
set.description: Remembers a value under a name that later steps read as '{{'vars.name'}}'.

wait.name: Wait
wait.description: Pauses the run for a number of seconds. Stop ends the pause at once.

http.name: HTTP request
http.description: Sends a request and keeps the status, the headers, the body and the JSON of the answer.

script.name: Script
script.description: Runs a script from the scripts folder, without a shell, and keeps its exit code and output.

notify.name: Notification
notify.description: Sends a message through the notifications module: to one channel, or to every ready channel when none is chosen. Old telegram steps load as this step with the telegram channel.

probe.name: Probe service
probe.description: Checks a service now, as its regular check would, and records the result.

status.name: Service status
status.description: Reads a service's current status without checking it again.

nothing.name: Do nothing
nothing.description: Leaves a branch empty on purpose: the run simply goes on.
nothing.example: If the NAS is up, do nothing; otherwise restart it.

transform.name: Transform
transform.description: Reshapes a value step by step: keeps matching items, turns each into something, sorts, groups, counts, or applies any filter. The result is the step's value.
transform.example: disks → failing ones → names → one line

automation.name: Start automation
automation.description: Queues one of your automations as if it was started by hand, with event fields you give; it may wait for its outcome.

log.name: Log
log.description: Writes a message into the run's trace, with values filled in. It never stops the run, whatever its level.

break.name: Leave loop
break.description: Ends the loop it is in at once; the run goes on after the loop. Only inside a loop.
break.example: If the NAS answered, leave the retry loop.

continue.name: Next pass
continue.description: Skips the rest of this pass and starts the loop's next one. Only inside a loop.
continue.example: Skip the TV and check the next host.

condition.label: Condition
condition.help: Rows of a value, an operator and another value; combine them with all or any.

else.label: Otherwise
else.help: Runs when it does not; may stay empty.

repeat.label: Times
repeat.help: Repeat the body this many times, from 1 to 100.

for_each.label: For each item of
for_each.help: A list, usually a JSON answer such as '{{'steps.list.json'}}'; each item is '{{'loop.item'}}'.

while.label: While
while.help: Repeat as long as this condition holds; it is checked before every pass.

max_iterations.label: At most, passes
max_iterations.help: A safety limit for “for each” and “while”, 100 at most.

branches.label: Branches
branches.help: 2 to 4 lists of steps that run together; their variables are merged in branch order.

workflow.label: Workflow
workflow.help: The workflow to run; it may not call this one back.

inputs.label: Inputs
inputs.help: A value for each input the called workflow declares.

outcome.label: Outcome
outcome.help: How the run ends in the journal.

reason.label: Reason
reason.help: Shown in the journal next to the outcome.

variable.label: Variable
variable.help: Lowercase letters, digits and _; later steps read it as '{{'vars.name'}}'.

json.label: JSON value
json.help: Use instead of Value to keep a number, a list or an object, for example '{{'steps.ping.json.items'}}'.

list.label: List
list.help: Each row is a template; a row that is only '{{'name'}}' keeps its type.

object.label: Dictionary
object.help: Each row is a key and a template; later steps read '{{'vars.name.key'}}'.

method.label: Method
method.help: GET reads, POST and PUT send, DELETE removes.

url.label: URL
url.help: An http:// or https:// address; templates are filled in.

headers.label: Headers
headers.help: Name and value pairs, for example Authorization = Bearer '{{'secrets.token'}}'.

body.label: Body
body.help: Text sent with the request; JSON is sent as application/json.

fail_on_error.label: Fail on status 400 and above
fail_on_error.help: Off lets the run go on and read the status itself.

response_sample.label: Answer structure
response_sample.help: An example of the JSON answer. Later steps get its keys as suggestions, such as steps.ping.json.state. The run does not check it.

script.label: Script
script.help: A file in the scripts folder with mode 0755 or stricter.

args.label: Arguments
args.help: Each argument is passed on its own, without a shell.

timeout_seconds.label: Time limit, seconds
timeout_seconds.help: From 1 to 3600; the script and everything it started are stopped after it.

env.label: Environment
env.help: Variables the script reads from its environment, such as $TARGET; each value is a template.

stdin.label: Standard input
stdin.help: A value written to the script's standard input as JSON, instead of the event fields; for example '{{'vars.report'}}'.

fail_on_error.label: Continue the run when the script fails
fail_on_error.help: On lets the run go on after a non-zero exit, with exit_code, stdout and stderr for later steps. Off, a non-zero exit fails the run.

text.label: Text
text.help: The message; templates are filled in.

title.label: Title
title.help: An optional first line in bold; templates are filled in.

channel.label: Channel
channel.help: A channel from the notifications page; empty sends to every ready channel.

service.label: Service
service.help: A service id, or a template such as '{{'inputs.service'}}'.

service.label: Service
service.help: A service id, or a template such as '{{'inputs.service'}}'.

input.label: Input
input.help: A template giving the value to reshape, such as '{{'steps.list.json.disks'}}'.

operations.label: Operations
operations.help: Applied in order, top to bottom; each card shows the value after it.

automation.label: Automation
automation.help: The automation to start; a workflow cannot start the automation that started it.

fields.label: Event fields
fields.help: Values the automation sees as its event fields, as '{{'service.id'}}', PORTAL_SERVICE_ID and on its standard input.

wait.label: Wait for it
wait.help: Wait for its run to finish and fail when it did not succeed.

message.label: Message
message.help: The text to write; templates are filled in.

level.label: Level
level.help: Info, warning or error: only the colour in the trace differs.

if.branch: The branch it took: then or else

loop.left_early: True when a “Leave loop” step ended it

workflow.vars: The variables the called workflow set

http.status: The HTTP status code, such as 200 or 404
http.body: The answer's text, the first 64 KiB
http.json: The answer as JSON, when it is JSON; add keys after it

probe.diagnosis: Why it failed, when it did

status.since: When the service entered that state

transform.value: The value after the last operation.

automation.run_id: The id of the run it queued
automation.outcome: How that run ended, when waited

log.message: The message as it was written

groups.event: The event that started the run

suggestions.jsonKey: Key {key} of the answer of {step}, as seen in the last run
suggestions.secret: Secret {name}, sent as it is and shown as *** in the journal
suggestions.secretUnset: This secret is not set yet; the step will fail

loop.item: The current item of the loop
loop.index: The number of the current pass, from 0

suggestions.sampleKey: Key {key} of the answer of {step}, from its answer structure

item.value: The current item of the list

reasons.unknownInput: {name} is not an input of this workflow
reasons.unknownVariable: no earlier step sets the variable {name}
reasons.outsideLoop: loop.{name} exists only inside a loop as loop.item and loop.index
reasons.notAValue: {name} is not a value a workflow knows
reasons.outsideTransform: {name} exists only inside a transform's filter and map
reasons.unreadableFilter: has a filter that cannot be read: {filter}
reasons.unknownFilter: names the filter {filter}, which does not exist
reasons.filterArgument: the argument {argument} of {filter} must be quoted text or a number, as its type says
reasons.notInPortal: {name} is not a value the portal offers

legend.title: How the editor works
legend.start: The top node holds the inputs and shows what starts the workflow.
legend.arrows: Arrows show the order steps run in; conditions fork and join again.
legend.plus: Press + on an arrow to add a step there, or drag a step onto another +.
legend.palette: The palette describes every kind of step with an example.
legend.completion: Type '{{' in any field to insert inputs, variables and results of earlier steps.

retry.title: Retry a request until it answers
retry.description: Asks an address up to three times, pausing between tries.

notify-down.title: Tell me when a service is down
notify-down.description: Probes a service and sends a notification when it is not up.

parallel-check.title: Check several services at once
parallel-check.description: Reads two statuses together and reports both.

daily-report.title: Daily report
daily-report.description: Builds a short text from statuses and sends it; start it from a schedule.

empty.title: Empty workflow
empty.description: Start from nothing and add steps with +.

split.description: Cuts text into a list at each separator.

slice.description: Part of a text or list, from start up to end; negative numbers count from the end.

starts_with.description: True when the text begins with the given text.

contains.description: True when the text holds the given text, or the list holds the value.

length.description: How many characters, items or keys.

default.description: The given value when this one is empty or missing.

round.description: Rounds to the given number of digits after the point.

first.description: The first item of a list.

last.description: The last item of a list.

join.description: Joins the items of a list into one text.

sort.description: Sorts a list: numbers by value, text alphabetically.

unique.description: Keeps the first of each repeated item.

pluck.description: Takes one key from every object of a list.

sum.description: Adds the numbers of a list.

min.description: The smallest number of a list.

max.description: The largest number of a list.

keys.description: The keys of an object, in order.

values.description: The values of an object, in the order of its keys.

get.label: get by key
get.description: The value at a key or a path such as a.b.0.

json.description: Writes any value as JSON text.

parse.description: Reads JSON text into a value.

filter.name: Keep the matching
filter.description: Keeps the items for which the condition holds; '{{'item'}}' is the current item.

map.name: Turn each into
map.description: Makes a new list from a template; '{{'item'}}' and '{{'index'}}' are the current item and its position.

sort_by.name: Sort by a key
sort_by.description: Sorts a list of objects by the value at a key, ascending or descending.

group_by.name: Group by a key
group_by.description: Makes an object of lists, one per value of the key.

count_by.name: Count by a key
count_by.description: Makes an object of counts, one per value of the key.

each.name: For each element
each.description: Runs its own chain of operations on every element and gives the list of results; inside it, '{{'item'}}' is the element.

notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.subtitle: Where messages about services and from workflows go, and which changes are announced.

test.failed: The test message was not delivered: {error}
test.unavailable: Set the channel up and switch the module on to send a test.

rules.title: What is announced
rules.description: Every ready channel receives these announcements.
rules.recovered: Announce when a service is up again

scriptArguments.title: Arguments
scriptArguments.doesNotFit: These arguments do not follow what the script declares, so they are kept as a list.
scriptArguments.headerProblems: The script's header has problems; those lines are ignored:

scripts.title: Scripts
scripts.subtitle: The scripts automations, webhooks and workflows run, in the scripts directory and its folders.
scripts.off: Editing scripts is switched off in the configuration file. Add this to it to switch it on:
scripts.missing: The scripts directory {directory} does not exist yet.
scripts.deleteDescription: The file is removed from the scripts directory.
scripts.deleteUsed: It is used by {users}; their next runs will be refused.
scripts.name: Name
scripts.leftOut: {count, plural, one {# entry deeper than one folder is not shown.} other {# entries deeper than one folder are not shown.}}
scripts.readOnly: Scripts can be changed only from inside your environments, so this page is read-only here.
scripts.choose: Choose a script to open it.

unreadable.binary: This file is not text, so it cannot be edited here.
unreadable.too-large: This file is larger than 256 KiB, so it cannot be edited here.
unreadable.link: This is a symbolic link, so it cannot be edited here.

scripts.conflict: The script changed since you opened it. Your text is kept.
scripts.leave: You have unsaved changes to this script. Leave anyway?
scripts.noDescription: The header has no @description line yet.

help.title: Header format
help.intro: Comment lines at the very top of the script, right after #!, describe it. The portal reads them without running the script and offers fields for them in automations, webhooks and workflow steps.

rows.description: One line saying what the script does.
rows.required: A positional argument; it is required.
rows.optional: A ? after the name makes a positional argument optional.
rows.option: An option with a type and a default.
rows.flag: An option without a type is a switch: it is passed alone when on.
rows.choice: A choice between fixed values, with a default.

help.rules: Types are text, number, flag, or choices such as a|b. The header ends at the first line that is not a comment; at most 64 lines and 32 arguments are read.
